column2: The Irish government has taken possession of the districts evacuated by the old administration. London refuses to recognise its independent foreign policy and has instructed the armed services to prepare an expedition. The cabinet seeks to bring Ireland under British protection, while the Irish ministers prepare to defend their sovereignty. The declaration must now pass from the cabinet to the commanders charged with carrying it into effect. The campaign will test whether the government can impose the authority it claims after the loss of the Cape.
Deliver the British declaration to Dublin.

Dublin and London have clarified the opposing claims to sovereignty. Irish ministers maintain the republic's independence, while the British cabinet demands a government subordinate to its protection. The armed services must receive orders identifying the opposing administration and the terms sought through the campaign. The dispute now lies between the two governments, whose decisions will determine whether the settlement survives or gives way to a British expedition.
Clarify the orders and confront the British demand.

The victory at the Cape has made Walvisbaai the republic's northern Atlantic gateway. Ministers have entered the adjoining unclaimed Namibian districts under republican protection, reserving their administration against competing overseas expeditions. Foreign-owned territory lies outside the mandate. The proclamation establishes responsibility for the frontier, but water supplies, roads and public stations require a separate funded programme. The raad can commission those works once its treasury and survey parties are ready. Its officials must record the existing communities and routes rather than treat the country as vacant merely because no recognised state has held its public offices.
Record the mandate and prepare the frontier programme.
Fund roads or district stations in the Namibian territories reserved through the Walvisbaai mandate. The programme requires peace, a funded treasury and the Atlantic gateway under republican control.

The funded survey parties have reported on the stations and routes that can be sustained from Walvisbaai. Engineers favour roads, wells and agricultural services that would keep produce and supplies moving through the arid districts. Commissioners instead urge a network of public offices and stations, recording local obligations and receiving newcomers. Either programme requires continued work after the ceremonies of occupation. The raad must choose which institutions the frontier will receive first.
Commission the roads, wells and agricultural services.
Establish the district offices and frontier stations.

Fund an expedition into the unclaimed Mashonaland districts beyond the northern routes. The column requires recognised continental diplomacy and passage through territory held by the republic or its northern protectorates. Governments already holding districts must be approached through the existing conventions.

The northern roads have become a central question of republican policy. Ministers seek a connected frontier from Bechuanaland towards the country beyond Mthwakazi, while merchants look to the eastern ports for supplies and export routes. The funded pioneer column will establish offices in districts without an existing recognised owner. It cannot seize the territory of a neighbouring government through a survey order. Those disputes remain matters for the protectorate conventions and campaigns debated by the raad. The commissioners must build routes, record local communities and sustain public authority in the districts they receive, turning a northern ambition into the practical work of government.
Dispatch the column and commission the northern districts.
